assertion.rationale: F4: layer-06 and layer-07 workflows cat their deployment manifests directly into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and upload them as artifacts, which on a public repo are readable without authentication. F4 is now CLOSED (Task 8). The `appInsightsConnectionString` output is deleted from infra/bicep/platform/main.bicep — nothing consumed it (apps/main.bicep reads the component as `existing`), so there is no longer a Bicep output carrying the App Insights ingestion key at all. The component also now sets `disableLocalAuth: true`, so the key that used to leak could no longer authorise ingestion on its own even if it were still published; mcp-tools and data-api's user-assigned identities are instead granted 'Monitoring Metrics Publisher' on the component (infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep, modules mcpAppInsightsGrant and dataApiAppInsightsGrant) and both apps' OpenTelemetry exporters now present a Microsoft Entra ID token via that identity when `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` is set (apps/mcp-tools/src/telemetry.ts, apps/data-api/src/telemetry/otel.ts), so ingestion keeps working without a key-based credential. Both layer-06-platform.yml and layer-07-apps.yml no longer `cat` the raw manifest into the job summary or upload it as an artifact — each writes a curated, explicitly non-sensitive subset of keys (resource group names, SQL/cost-export account names, container app names, image digests, the three externally-ingress FQDNs) instead. verification/tests/no-secret-outputs.Tests.ps1 regression-guards both: no Bicep output name may suggest a connection string, key, or secret, and no workflow may `cat` a manifest into the job summary. Overall status is now CLOSED: this control's only contributor (F4) is closed. This control has no other open contributor (checked: no other finding in compliance/findings/2026-08-26-prepublication-review.md cites 3.1.3).

recommendation: None outstanding for this control. (Deleting the appInsightsConnectionString output, disabling local App Insights auth with a matching Monitoring Metrics Publisher grant and Microsoft Entra credential wiring, and replacing the raw-manifest cat/artifact with a curated summary, Task 8, are all DONE.) A regression here — the connection-string output reintroduced, disableLocalAuth reverted without a matching credential change, or a workflow cat-ing a manifest into the job summary again — would reopen this control; verification/tests/no-secret-outputs.Tests.ps1 catches both the output and the workflow shape of that regression.
